gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.summary: 6/6 DAMAGED non-OLMo arms land at/below their own best-constant floor 0.2689. Llama-2 k8 0.2415 (-2.74pp), Llama-3 k8 0.2329 (-3.60), Qwen3 k8 0.2286 (-4.03), Llama-2 k12 0.2295 (-3.94), Llama-3 k12 0.2527 (-1.62), Qwen3 k12 0.2300 (-3.89). gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.mechanism_finding: The collapse ROUTE differs by family but the OUTCOME does not. Non-OLMo damaged arms become constant-letter emitters with NEAR-ZERO exact ties (Llama-2 k12 is 100.0% modal with 0.00% ties; Qwen3 k12 is 99.1% modal with 0.03% ties). OLMo damaged arms reach the same place via 30.64% exact ties + argmax index tie-breaking. So ties are ONE road, not THE mechanism -- this over-determines the gate-3 refutation.
gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.content_also_fails: every damaged arm has content_norm within +/-3pp of its letter accuracy and both hover at their floors -- switching interface does NOT rescue a damaged arm

gate1_depth_curve.verdict: THE TWO INTERFACES HAVE DIFFERENT FUNCTIONAL FORMS -- letter is a STEP function of depth, content_norm is SMOOTH and MONOTONE
gate1_depth_curve.ran: 2026-08-08/09, four families across .21/.73/.82; 58 arms x 14042 items, thresholds pinned to a single layer
gate1_depth_curve.headline: Letter accuracy sits pinned at its 0.2689 floor over a wide depth range, then jumps 27-48pp at ONE layer, then plateaus. Content_norm over the SAME forward passes rises smoothly and monotonically with no jump anywhere. At the layer where Qwen3 letter moves +48.0pp (k24 0.2297 -> k25 0.7099), Qwen3 content moves +1.4pp (0.3045 -> 0.3180).

thresholds_pinned.qwen3_8b_36L: k24->k25, +48.0pp. Pinned at 0.2295-0.2301 for k=4..24 -- twenty depths agreeing within 0.06pp
thresholds_pinned.relative_depth: thresholds at k/L = 0.69 / 0.56 / 0.59 -- past the midpoint in all three, but n=3, NOT a law

gate1_depth_curve.llama2_anomaly: letter NON-MONOTONE (k16 0.3289 +6.0pp -> k20 0.3054 -> k24 0.2723 +0.3pp back at floor -> k28 0.4315) while content over the same range is STRICTLY monotone (0.2650->0.2877->0.3139->0.3548). The non-monotonicity is in the readout, not the model. Gap-fill k=8,12,18,22,26 in flight on .21. Also: Llama-2's k28 letter 0.4315 already exceeds its INTACT 0.4100, so its plateau is at intact level -- it is a weak-model case, not a damage case.
gate1_depth_curve.why_it_matters: Supplies a mechanism-free version of A01's protocol argument. Below threshold the letter interface IS a constant predictor; above it, a competent one. Averaging arms that straddle the threshold mixes two regimes. Any damage-scaling regression on letter accuracy that includes sub-threshold rungs is fitting a step, and its slope is an artifact of how many rungs land on each side. This also EXPLAINS the 6/6 damaged result: those arms were keep8/keep12, deep inside every family's sub-threshold range.
gate1_depth_curve.does_not_show: no mechanism (tie explanation stays triple-falsified, this does not resurrect it); nothing about HEALED arms (all arms here are truncation-only); no per-subject breakdown

gate2_second_mc_benchmark.summary: On non-MMLU MC the interface/floor failure DOES reproduce. BoolQ's construct-appropriate null is 0.6217 (always-B), not 0.5: keep12/keep10/keep8 all sit BELOW it on the raw-LL interface and keep14 is n.s. (p=0.20) -> 4/6 arms indistinguishable from a constant predictor while their nominal 0.59-0.64 look 'passing' against a 0.50 chance line. gate2_second_mc_benchmark.negative_control: winogrande is structurally degenerate (both options share the continuation -> identical norm_lens, acc == acc_norm exactly, 100% tie rate). Cannot serve as an interface case; report as a control, not evidence.
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.clean_cases: CommonsenseQA (5-way) and SocialIQA (3-way): all 6 arms significantly ABOVE their constant-letter nulls on both interfaces -- the 'not everything collapses' side of the protocol.

gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.headline_3_fp32_makes_damaged_arms_more_: modal concentration rises under fp32 on every damaged arm: keep10 D 60.1->65.1%, keep12 D 49.3->61.3%, keep8 C 48.8->55.9%. ADDED 2026-08-09 -- the input-blind null A01 recommends is itself UNDER-SPECIFIED, and its convention degree of freedom reverses verdicts. On MMLU the longest-option null takes values 0.196126/0.281085/0.282154/0.284450/0.453710 under the five defensible tie conventions (wrong/first/last/split/credit); 34.22% of items have a tie, 13.37% have all four tied. Under 'credit' 5 of 6 OLMo-2 arms flip from 'above the null' to 'significantly BELOW the null'. So the protocol must be 'report a construct-appropriate null AND print its convention'. This is A01's protocol applied reflexively and is the strongest claim it owns outright. The same null is ALSO tokenizer-dependent across families (Llama-2 0.2757 / Qwen3 0.2833 / Llama-3 0.2847 / OLMo-2 0.2845 under the same split convention), so cross-family content comparisons need per-family nulls.
family_specific_not_general: The collapse MECHANISM. OLMo-2 gets there via exact bf16 ties (30.64% on keep8) resolved by argmax index bias; Llama/Qwen get there via direct modal collapse with near-zero ties. Same destination, different road.

On HEALTHY strong models the letter interface is substantially BETTER than the label-free content interface (+13 to +23pp on OLMo-2 base, Llama-3, Qwen3). So 'content is the fair interface' is not a general statement about MC interfaces -- it is a statement about damaged models.

novelty_check_2026_08_09.clause_tested_verbatim: '论文只能退化为已有 similarity-null 方法的案例集合。' -- i.e. the clause fires IFF everything A01 contributes reduces to applying already-published SIMILARITY-NULL machinery to new data. It is NOT a generic 'is anything novel' test.
novelty_check_2026_08_09.rationale: Two independent reasons. (1) The clause is scoped to the similarity-null (C3/representation) leg, which A01 already concedes it does not own -- but A01's surviving load-bearing findings are all on the MC-ACCURACY construct: four-family letter collapse to at/below the best-constant floor under damage, letter-as-step-function-of-depth vs content-as-smooth over the same forward passes, the six-arm fp32 refutation of the tie mechanism, and the newly tabulated convention-sensitivity of the longest-option null. None is an instance of a similarity-null method. (2) No verified prior work covers that scope. Closest is Balepur et al. ACL 2024 main, which argues for stronger-than-chance baselines in MCQA -- but on INTACT models, as a dataset-artifact claim, with no damage axis, no depth curve, no per-arm floor validity gate, and no convention analysis of the null.

novelty_check_2026_08_09.kill_definition: Clause 3 fires iff a paper (or the union of existing similarity-null papers) already does A01's scope, i.e. (1) uses an input-blind / best-constant null as a per-arm VALIDITY GATE that disqualifies an arm from cross-arm comparison, (2) on structurally DAMAGED models (not intact ones), (3) across more than one model family, AND (4) shows the interface/readout choice interacts with the damage. No candidate satisfies any two of these four simultaneously. Balepur et al. satisfies a weak form of (1) only, on intact models. Overlap on the RECOMMENDATION ('use stronger baselines') is not preemption of the SCOPE.
